text:
alex: Heads-up — we've been seeing tenants flip between v1/v2 routing frequently during traffic spikes. affinity hash looks noisy, debounce seems too short. anyone seen this pattern? /cc @telemetry-bot :thinking:
priya: saw that on prod earlier, noticed a burst at 03:12 where ~12% of requests switched to v1 for ~20s before switching back. logs attached in thread.
sam: hmm, is that the console-driven pin expiry kicking in? could be pin TTL + bursty new tokens.
jo: not a pin TTL, we traced a case where header negotiation timed out and fallback returned v1. fallback path has lower debounce.
emma: console shows lots of "route_pin=auto" churn in the dashboard around that time. UX currently expires pins after 5m of inactivity — maybe too aggressive for spiky workloads.
alex: config we used for the test: 
```json
{"affinity_debounce_ms": 5000, "pin_ttl_secs": 300, "fallback_window_ms": 1000}
```
alex: the quick fallback_window_ms seems suspicious. if fallback path flips quickly it defeats user expectation of stable version.
priya: telemetry summary: 
- 03:11:58 -> 03:12:22 increased 95th latency for v2
- 03:12:00 -> 03:12:20 12% of tokens routed to v1
- spike correlated with a single tenant with 7k reqs/min
telemetry-bot: (auto) linked stats -> https://internal.metrics/affinity/1759600123 :bar_chart:
sam: two options: raise affinity_debounce_ms to 30s, or make fallback path require N consecutive failures (debounce on errors not just time).
jo: prefer error-count debounce. Time-only debounce impacts legitimate rebalances. error-count gives us signal that v2 is unhealthy for that tenant.
riley: SRE concern: long debounce (30s) could delay failover for real regressions. we need a hybrid: short failover on sustained error rate, but sticky routing when errors are transient.
emma: UX ask: expose a "stability window" on the console per-tenant so customers can tune (with safe bounds). show current pin TTL + debounce in route details.
priya: telemetry support: we can add a per-tenant time-series for routing flips (v2->v1->v2) and alert when flip-rate > X/min.
alex: proposal: implement hybrid policy: 1) require 3 consecutive 5xx responses within 2s to trigger immediate fallback; 2) maintain post-fallback debounce_ms=20s to avoid oscillation; 3) console shows a compact "recent flips" sparkline and a one-click override to "lock to v2 for 10m".
jo: Agreed. also add a metric for "pin override usage" so we can see how often console fixes are used.
sam: I'll sketch the config flags: 
```
route_policy: {
  fallback_error_count: 3,
  fallback_error_window_ms: 2000,
  post_fallback_debounce_ms: 20000,
  max_debounce_ms: 120000
}
```
priya: will add telemetry counters: routing_flip_count, last_flip_ts, flip_cohort_tenant. can we sample flips at 1% for payload inspection?
emma: sampling is ok if opt-in per-tenant. show warning about sensitive data.
riley: ops checklist: add runbook for rapid rollback if flip-rate spikes after change; notify oncall and disable auto-fallback if we see global outage.
alex: timeline: sam implements policy change + feature flag by EOD tomorrow, telemetry adds flip metrics and alert by Friday, console UX mock by next sprint.
priya: creating a short-lived gauge alert: flip_rate > 5/min for tenant -> P3 page to #eng-oncall.
jo: one more corner: legacy clients that only speak v1 may be mis-tagged by header negotiation. we should add a client-compat header whitelist to avoid forcing them through fallback path.
sam: noted. will add whitelist check before counting errors for fallback.
alex: thanks all — feel free to DM if you want to pair on tests. :thumbsup:
telemetry-bot: (auto) thread archived to project "routing-stability"
